content:
Algebra makes its official debut in Class 6 — variables, expressions, matchstick patterns and simple equations. Olympiad papers use it to separate rule-followers from pattern-spotters. Here is what the IMO Class 6 algebra chapter tests, with a free 10-question test.

What the Class 6 Maths Olympiad Algebra chapter tests

  • Variables and matchstick/dot patterns
  • Writing expressions from statements
  • Evaluating expressions by substitution
  • Solving simple equations (one inverse step)

Key facts your child should know

  • A variable stands for ANY number — that is why rules written with n work everywhere.
  • "5 more than x" is x + 5; "one-fourth of p" is p/4.
  • If x = 4, then 3x + 2 = 14 — substitute, then follow BODMAS.
  • Solve by inverse operations and CHECK by substituting back.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Writing "7 less than y" as 7 − y instead of y − 7.
  • Treating 3x as 3 + x.
  • Skipping the substitute-back check on equations.

faq.a: A letter that stands for a number that can change — writing 3n + 1 describes the stick count for EVERY number of squares n at once.
